passages.provision_quote: (2) The large load customer commits to significant and meaningful financial assurances that must: (A) include reimbursement by the large load customer of at least eighty percent (80%) of the project costs reasonably allocable to the large load customer; and (B) afford protections for the energy utility's existing and future customers from project costs reasonably allocable to the large load customer regardless of whether the large load customer ultimately takes service in the anticipated amount and within the anticipated time frame.
passages.note: The large load customer chapter requires cost-reimbursement and ratepayer protections while also creating an expedited, deadline-driven commission review process, mixing rung 3 and rung 4 elements.
The IGA bill-tracking page confirms Soliday authored HB 1007 and that it was signed into law as Public Law 217.

rows.reasoning: Soliday authored HB 1007 (2025), signed into law, which creates an expedited generation-resource-plan process for utilities serving 'large load customers' (data centers meeting size and investment thresholds) that requires the customer to reimburse at least eighty percent of project costs and protects existing and future customers from cost shifting, while also imposing strict commission deadlines. This mixes rung 3's 'impact assessments, energy cost-sharing agreements... before approval' with rung 4's 'streamlined permitting while requiring transparency about projected energy demand and rate impacts' without fully matching either rung's clauses, so the record shows a pro-development-with-conditions direction but does not separate the two rungs.
needs_source: Soliday's own floor statement or sponsor explanation of HB 1007 tying the EGR plan process specifically to streamlined permitting (rung 4) or to cost-sharing/impact-assessment gatekeeping (rung 3)
